cards.title: Auto theft in Canada falls 18% but organized crime is getting smarter, warns Équité
cards.claim: Équité reports national vehicle thefts fell in 2025 yet claims stay near $900 million a year, with organized groups shifting toward finance fraud using synthetic identities.

stat.what: National private passenger vehicle thefts and annual theft claims cost, Équité Association

cards.relevance: Gives the national theft base rate against which a broker book that is 86% theft claims looks anomalous, and shows organized crime also exploits insurance and financing channels.
cards.limit: Trade-press summary of the Équité report; says nothing about broker-originated policies.

cards.title: Auto theft is down 18%, but organized crime is finding new ways to export stolen vehicles
cards.claim: Theft risk is concentrated in particular models, and the report calls theft high-reward and low-risk; model mix of an insured book can therefore legitimately lift theft claim share.

stat.what: Share of insured vehicles stolen for the highest-frequency model in Équité's 2025 list

cards.relevance: Challenges a pure-fraud reading: if B07 sold mostly high-theft models (keyless-entry SUVs), elevated theft share and severity have a non-fraud explanation worth testing.
cards.limit: Model-level rate is one data point; cannot explain 60 theft claims within weeks of inception or 0 denials.

cards.title: GTA police bust organized insurance fraud scheme network (Project Outsource)
cards.claim: Peel police allege tow-company-linked groups staged collisions and inflated repair and service costs billed to insurers, using coercion to control scenes.

stat.what: Outcome of Peel Regional Police Project Outsource, June 2025

cards.relevance: Documents that organized, repeat claim schemes against Ontario insurers are real and police-confirmed, so a ring-driven cluster is plausible.
cards.limit: Staged collisions and tow fraud, not theft claims or broker involvement; allegations unproven in court.

cards.title: Ontario tow-sector probe shines spotlight on systemic auto insurance fraud
cards.claim: Court filings in a related case list many fraud charges against insurers and the article notes Aviva's suspected staged-collision cases rose nearly fourfold in 2025.

stat.what: Year-over-year rise in suspected staged-collision cases identified by Aviva Canada

cards.relevance: Shows insurers are seeing sharp, repeated-pattern fraud growth that hits loss ratios when the same scheme recurs across files.
cards.limit: Staged collisions, not theft; Aviva-reported figure with no denominator; charges are allegations.

cards.title: Beware of ghost brokers
cards.claim: Aviva describes ghost brokers as people posing as brokers who sell coverage they cannot place, with bargain social-media pricing and e-transfer payments as warning signs.
cards.relevance: Defines the policy-side fraud typology: policies that look valid but may be counterfeit or built on false details, a possible route for B07 policies.
cards.limit: Victim-side consumer warning; ghost brokers are unlicensed outsiders, whereas B07 is a contracted broker.

cards.title: Peel police: Economic pressure creates opening for insurance fraudsters
cards.claim: Police allege a former brokerage employee sold fake auto policies for over two years, but say they see no wider trend of ex-brokers committing fraud.

stat.what: Incidents police identified in the alleged fake-policy case

cards.relevance: A recent Ontario example of agent-assisted policy fraud, tempered by police saying it is not a broad trend.
cards.limit: Single alleged case about fake policies, not insured claims; unproven allegations.

cards.title: Red flags in business interruption claims (Claims Journal)
cards.claim: A claim shortly after policy activation, after raised coverage, or just before expiry warrants scrutiny, but the author stresses flags call for investigation rather than prove fraud and most claims are legitimate.
cards.relevance: Supports using early-claim timing as a screening flag while cautioning that timing alone is not proof, so B07 needs corroborating indicators.
cards.limit: US business-interruption context by a forensic accountant, no time window given, no Canadian personal-lines data.

cards.title: ML/TF indicators: Life insurance companies, brokers and agents
cards.claim: FINTRAC lists multiple transactions kept below reporting thresholds, and cancelling insurance soon after purchase, as suspicion indicators for insurance brokers and agents.
cards.relevance: Regulatory precedent in Canadian insurance that amounts clustered under a threshold are a recognised red flag.
cards.limit: Anti-money-laundering guidance on client transactions, not claims; page date not captured; only first 100,000 characters read.

cards.title: Business rules alone are not enough to fight insurance fraud
cards.claim: Fixed referral cutoffs are easy to game because a fraudster can learn the insurer's limit and keep every claim under it, bypassing investigator referral.
cards.relevance: Directly describes the mechanism that would explain about 46 of 70 B07 claims falling between 8,000 and 9,999.
cards.limit: Vendor-authored opinion piece with no measured bunching data.

cards.title: 3 Warning Signs of Adverse Selection
cards.claim: Rising loss ratios and loss costs are the first sign of adverse selection, and blaming rivals rather than examining one's own risk selection is a common mistake.
cards.relevance: Offers a non-fraud reading: rapid growth through a new channel can attract underpriced risk, producing a high loss ratio without intentional deceit.
cards.limit: Generic commercial-lines opinion piece, old, not about broker programs or early claims.

cards.title: AM Best Report Cites MGA's Role in Insurer Insolvencies
cards.claim: AM Best says some MGAs wrote unprofitable business to raise commissions and insurers need checks and balances and awareness of what delegated partners write.

stat.value: 13 insolvencies; all but one gave >=96% of premium to MGAs
stat.what: AM Best review of property insurer insolvencies since 2017

cards.relevance: Shows commission-driven volume growth through delegated distributors is a recognised insurer-failure risk, supporting tighter controls on B07.
cards.limit: US property MGAs, mostly Florida; some industry figures dispute the link; B07 is an independent broker.

cards.title: Managing General Agent's Agreement, Alfa Vision / Vision Insurance Group (SEC exhibit)
cards.claim: A real contract lets the insurer terminate on a loss-ratio breach, end immediately for fraud, suspend binding authority, and audit records, including semi-annual on-site audits.

stat.what: Claims-incurred loss-ratio trigger for termination on 30 days' notice (premium above $2M)

cards.relevance: Concrete precedent for loss-ratio triggers and suspension of authority that could be applied to B07 at a ratio of 4.3.
cards.limit: One 2005 US MGA contract, not Canadian broker terms.

cards.title: FSRA finds gaps in insurers' oversight of MGAs, agents
cards.claim: Ontario's regulator found insurers' proactive reviews covered a tiny share of agents and several lacked formal MGA or agent reviews, linking weak oversight to conduct problems.

stat.what: Share of active agents covered by insurers' own proactive reviews (8 insurers, life and health)

cards.relevance: Establishes that Canadian regulators expect insurers to own oversight of distributors, and that thin monitoring is common.
cards.limit: Life and health sector, self-reported survey; says nothing about P&C broker suspension triggers.

cards.title: Équité Association launches insurance crime detection platform
cards.claim: Équité's EQ Insights consortium platform shares intelligence among member insurers to predict and prevent fraud, and insurance crime is estimated to cost Canadians billions annually.

stat.what: Estimated annual cost of insurance-related crime to Canadians

cards.relevance: Sizes the cost of fraud and points to the shared-intelligence channel for checking whether B07 insureds or vehicles appear at other insurers.
cards.limit: Secondary press report with a wide range and no methodology; publication date not captured.
